title: Grade 3 Science — Wed, May 20
description: Air and Water — Properties and Importance — Last Week Day 3
subject: science

questions.question: What gas in air do we need to breathe?
questions.explanation: Oxygen (about 21% of air) is essential for breathing. Our cells need oxygen to release energy.

questions.question: Which gas makes up most of the air (about 78%)?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of air. Oxygen is about 21%. The rest is argon, carbon dioxide, and other gases.

questions.question: Air has weight. TRUE or FALSE?
questions.explanation: TRUE. Air has mass and weight — this creates air pressure. The atmosphere pushes down on us with about 1 kg per cm².

questions.question: What does moving air (wind) cause?
options: Kites to fly, waves in water, windmills to spin
questions.explanation: Moving air (wind) creates energy — it can fly kites, create ocean waves, and spin wind turbines to generate electricity.

questions.question: Water is essential for life because:
options: All living things need it for survival
questions.explanation: All living things — plants, animals, fungi, bacteria — need water to survive. Life as we know it cannot exist without water.

questions.question: What are the three forms of water found in nature?
questions.explanation: Water exists as ice (solid), liquid water, and water vapour (gas) — all found naturally on Earth.

questions.question: What is the main source of fresh water on Earth?
options: Glaciers and ice caps, rivers and lakes
questions.explanation: Most fresh water is locked in glaciers and ice caps. Rivers, lakes, and groundwater supply most of what we use daily.

questions.question: Air pollution is caused by:
options: Smoke from factories and vehicles releasing harmful gases
questions.explanation: Air pollution comes from burning fuels in factories and vehicles, releasing harmful gases like carbon monoxide and sulphur dioxide.

questions.question: Water at 100°C:
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100°C (at sea level) and rapidly turns to water vapour (steam).

questions.question: Which property of air makes it useful for tyres and balloons?
options: Air can be compressed (squeezed into a small space)
questions.explanation: Air can be compressed — we pump compressed air into tyres, footballs, and balloons, where it pushes outward.

questions.question: How can we reduce water pollution?
options: Avoid throwing chemicals and rubbish into water sources
questions.explanation: We reduce water pollution by not dumping chemicals or rubbish into rivers and oceans, and by treating wastewater.

questions.question: What do fish need that is dissolved in water?
questions.explanation: Fish breathe dissolved oxygen through their gills — they don't breathe air like us but need oxygen dissolved in water.

questions.question: Where does most of the clean drinking water come from?
questions.explanation: Our drinking water mostly comes from rivers, lakes, and underground sources (wells/aquifers), which is then treated to make it safe.

questions.question: What is acid rain?
options: Rain made acidic by air pollution (SO₂, NO₂)
Rain that falls in winter only
questions.explanation: Acid rain forms when sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from burning fuels mix with water in clouds, making the rain acidic. It harms plants and buildings.

questions.question: What simple step can save water at home?
options: Leave taps running while brushing teeth
Turn off the tap while brushing teeth
Fill up the bath every day
questions.explanation: Turning off the tap while brushing saves about 6 litres of water per minute — a simple habit that makes a big difference.
